pick.headline: US-Soviet talks on intermediate-range missiles open in Geneva
pick.summary: On 30 November 1981 the United States and the Soviet Union opened negotiations in Geneva on intermediate-range nuclear forces in Europe.
pick.significance: The talks followed Reagan's 'zero option' proposal; they broke down in 1983 when Pershing II deployment began, but resumed and produced the INF Treaty in 1987.
pick.fbis: The East Europe report of 30 November 1981 carried bloc commentary backing the Soviet proposal for a moratorium on new intermediate-range missiles during the Geneva negotiations beginning that Monday.

alternates.headline: Uruguayans reject the military's constitution
alternates.summary: On 30 November 1980 voters in Uruguay rejected, in a plebiscite, a draft constitution proposed by the ruling military that would have entrenched the armed forces' role in government.
alternates.significance: The defeat was a rare instance of a military regime losing its own referendum, and began Uruguay's slow return to civilian rule in 1985.
alternates.fbis: The Latin America report of 1 December 1980 listed Argentine reaction under the heading that Argentines voiced satisfaction at the Uruguayan vote.
